items.title: An operation per editor verb, with the UI and the agent both dispatching it

must_fix.evidence: The registry has one operation (map_set_settings) and 128 actions are on the unmigrated allowlist. The brief asks for one workflow first, with the allowlist shrinking.

items.title: The kit's library and policy are re-read by a full project reload, which is slow and loses the open map

must_fix.evidence: watch.rs::adopt re-opens the whole project for a library change, because only Project::open knows how to merge every bound kit. A per-kit re-read would be better.

items.title: The operation log has a single-writer assumption, so two agents would claim the same sequence number

must_fix.evidence: ops.rs::next_seq counts the lines in the log, and the MCP server and the editor are separate processes that could both append. An advisory file lock would fix it.

items.title: Enclosure wish and weight are hard-coded in the editor, so an author who wants more enclosed rooms edits Rust

must_fix.evidence: editor.rs ENCLOSURE_WISH = 0.25 and ENCLOSURE_WEIGHT = 200 are not in rules.ron, so they are not authored and cannot be tuned without a rebuild.

items.title: No crate in this workspace is published to crates.io, so the first publication is undecided

must_fix.evidence: cargo info for all seven crates says 'could not find ... in registry'. There is no published baseline, so no release can be made and no pre-publish gate has a version to check against.

items.evidence: cargo info bevy_emerge_core@0.1.0 (and the other six)

items.title: The chooser's new-map dialog writes name, bounds, origin and note directly, outside the registry

must_fix.evidence: chooser.rs:5907-5910 (write_settings) and chooser.rs:662 (write_bash) write the map's settings without dispatching map_set_settings. They are a different subject -- a new map with no open map -- and the honest claim is that one operation has two front ends, not that every verb does.

items.title: The human cannot undo a map-settings change: Cmd+Z takes back placements only, and no UI reverts by operation id
items.evidence: Agent side shipped as emerge_undo_operation (39ab825). User problem: a size-field typo is fixed by retyping; frequency: every settings edit; saving: one keystroke; risk: Cmd+Z then has two histories unless it dispatches ops::undo.

items.title: Frame time is unmeasurable through MCP and unreliable on a shared machine
items.evidence: emerge_state has no frame clock; bevy_debugger/status tick counting gave 33.1 / 20.2 / 67.2 ms medians at load 2 agents / idle / load-avg 30.8. A per-frame CPU-time diagnostic in emerge_state would separate the editor from the machine.

items.title: Signature-reading ratchets cannot see resources inside #[derive(SystemParam)] bundles
items.evidence: B-005 introduced 32 bundles; the_sweep_is_finished and every_resource_says_what_a_door_does_to_it read fn signatures, so a bare Res in a bundle used by an on_* observer would pass. on_shelf_click was kept unbundled for this reason; the ratchets should resolve bundle fields.
